packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-02 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

EXPOSURE / RULES STATEMENT
Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or an earlier reading of
this fragment. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..006 of this packet. No web,
search, catalogue or edition was used. I have not tried to identify work or
author, and nothing below is supplied from memory of any text.

1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only)

Observations
- A narrow horizontal parchment strip photographed on a black ground, two faces:
  image-001 = overview of face A (tiles image-002 left, image-003 right);
  image-004 = overview of face B (tiles image-005 left, image-006 right).
  Writing is upright on both overviews.
- The strip preserves a wide blank band above the writing (apparently an upper
  margin) and then only the first two lines of each of two columns, with the
  tops of a third line along the cut lower edge. So each face shows the head of
  two columns, 2 lines + traces each.
- Short lines that do not fill the column width, each beginning with a capital
  that is set apart to the left of the rest of the line and touched with a red
  stroke; the remainder of the line starts after a small gap. No rubrics,
  running titles, enlarged initials, glosses or underlining are visible.
- Gothic bookhand (textualis), brown-black ink, in places abraded (worst on
  face A col. a line 1 and the right end of face B col. b). Abbreviation strokes
  for nasals and a superscript hook for -er are used.
- Physical: horizontal slits near both ends at the level of line 1, several
  small holes, a vertical crease/tear and a puckered hole near the centre
  between the columns; left and right ends of the strip are trimmed obliquely.
  Face A shows letters in the far left margin beside col. a (a red-touched
  capital and, below it, strokes turned sideways) that look like offset or
  remains of other writing; I could not read them as words.

Tentative interpretation (not observation)
- The line structure (one short line per verse, detached initial letters) and
  the apparent end-rhymes suggest verse in a Dutch/Low-German type vernacular,
  written in two columns. The strip looks like binding waste cut across the top
  of a leaf. Which face is recto and the order of the four columns cannot be
  fixed from two lines each; if the leaf was read in the usual way the order
  would be face-x col. a, col. b, then the other face col. a, col. b, but about
  a whole column of text is missing between each pair of surviving couplets.

2. SPANS SELECTED / UNREAD
All visible writing was read: two lines in each of the four columns. The third
line in each column is cut through horizontally and only letter-tops remain;
those are reported as traces, not read. The marginal marks left of face A col. a
are unread.

Conventions: abbreviation marks kept (õ, ñ, ĩ = stroke over the letter;
' = superscript hook); proposed expansions in ( ); "?" follows an uncertain
reading; the detached initial is given first, separated by a space. Line numbers
are counted from the top of each tile.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
FACE A (image-001), COLUMN a  - tile image-002
------------------------------------------------------------------------
image-002 l.1   E nde daer toe? goeden? wijn?
                [abraded; "nde daer" fairly clear, "toe" and "goeden" read from
                 partial letters, final word a run of minims with w-, "wijn" or
                 "win"]
image-002 l.2   S? i ghingen metten bliden sin?
                [the initial is a sideways-looking letter in the margin, S? ;
                 "ghingen" could be "ghingen"/"ghmgen" (minims); "bliden" could
                 be "bliden"/"bleden"; last word "sin"/"sijn"]
image-002 l.3   [traces only: tops of letters, something like "... vele? ...";
                 not read]

Left margin beside l.1-3: a capital resembling E with red touch at l.1 level and
sideways strokes below; [illegible] as text.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
FACE A, COLUMN b  - tile image-003
------------------------------------------------------------------------
(The left edge of image-003 repeats the ends of col. a l.1-2: overlap, not new
text.)

image-003 l.1   V oer den cõ? (coninc?) sijn? si ghecomen?
                [initial V/W touched red; "oer den" clear; then "co" with a
                 superscript sign; "sijn si" from minims; last word begins
                 "ghe-" and ends "-en", middle rubbed]
image-003 l.2   D ie k'nige? (coninge?) knielde vele saen?
                [after "D ie" a word beginning with k/c and an abbreviation,
                 ending "-ge"; "knielde" fairly clear; "vele" clear; last word
                 "saen"/"scien", rubbed]
image-003 l.3   [traces only: a few letter-tops at the cut edge; not read]

------------------------------------------------------------------------
FACE B (image-004), COLUMN a  - tile image-005
------------------------------------------------------------------------
image-005 l.1   S al ic bliuen ongehangen
                [clear. Initial S with red stroke; "alic" written together]
image-005 l.2   E ñ (ende) gine sult mi nz? (niet?) ontgãgẽ (ontgangen)
                ["gine" = g-i-n-e as written; the word before "ontgãgẽ" is a
                 short abbreviated form of two or three strokes, read "nz"/"niet"
                 with doubt]
image-005 l.3   [cut away; nothing legible in this tile]

------------------------------------------------------------------------
FACE B, COLUMN b  - tiles image-005 (right edge) and image-006
------------------------------------------------------------------------
(The right edge of image-005 shows "D es" and "E m.." = beginning of the lines
below: overlap, not new text.)

image-006 l.1   D es hadden si wond' (wonder) groot
                [initial D touched red; "groot" written with a round double-o
                 form, last letter t]
image-006 l.2   E ñ? die? coniginne? al bloot?
                [the letters after E are rubbed: I see "nne"/"ñ die" then
                 "conĩgine" with a stroke over the middle, then "al bloot"
                 ("blaot"/"bloot"); faint further marks to the right of "bloot"
                 look like show-through or offset, not read]
image-006 l.3   E? [traces only: tops of about five words along the cut edge,
                 ending perhaps in "...s? seide?"; not read with confidence]

3. LIMITATIONS
- Only two full lines survive at the head of each column; everything below is
  cut away. No connected span longer than a couplet exists on the fragment, so
  the brief's request for ten-line spans cannot be met from this leaf.
- Face A is noticeably more abraded than face B; face A col. a line 1 and the
  ends of face A col. b lines 1-2 are the weakest readings. Face B col. a
  line 1 and col. b line 1 are the most secure.
- Minim sequences (n/u/i/m, "ghingen", "sijn", "wijn") are intrinsically
  ambiguous in this script and are marked.
- Column order and recto/verso are not established. The third lines could
  probably be recovered if an adjacent strip from the same leaf exists; a
  raking-light or multispectral image of face A would help with the rubbed
  words and with the marginal marks at the far left.
- This is an unverified image reading. Expansions in parentheses are proposals.
